Some teams agree not to use parts of the `jest` object: no module mocks, no fake timers, no spies. This rule reports the methods you list, with your own message if you give one, so the agreement does not depend on review.

The rule does nothing until you give it a list.

## Examples

These examples restrict `advanceTimersByTime` and `spyOn`.

Reported:

{/* bad {"count": 2, "options": [{"advanceTimersByTime": null, "spyOn": "Pass the dependency in instead of spying on it"}]} */}
```ts
import { expect, jest, test } from "bun:test";

test("retries after a second", () => {
  const send = jest.spyOn(mailer, "send");
  retry(send);
  jest.advanceTimersByTime(1000);
  expect(send).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
});
```

Not reported:

{/* good {"options": [{"advanceTimersByTime": null, "spyOn": "Pass the dependency in instead of spying on it"}]} */}
```ts
import { expect, jest, test } from "bun:test";

test("retries once", () => {
  const send = jest.fn();
  retry(send);
  expect(send).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
});
```

`vi` is checked the same way as `jest`:

{/* bad {"options": [{"spyOn": "Pass the dependency in instead of spying on it"}]} */}
```ts
import { vi } from "bun:test";

const send = vi.spyOn(mailer, "send");
```

Only methods of `jest` and `vi` are checked. The `spyOn` and `mock` functions that `"bun:test"` exports are not:

{/* good {"options": [{"spyOn": "Pass the dependency in instead of spying on it"}]} */}
```ts
import { spyOn } from "bun:test";

const send = spyOn(mailer, "send");
```

## Options

One object. Each key is the name of a method. The value is the message to report.

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"bun:test/no-restricted-jest-methods" = ["error", { spyOn = "Pass the dependency in instead of spying on it" }]
```

In a JSON or JavaScript config, `null` in place of the message gives the default message: ``Use of `spyOn` is not allowed``.
